ai.description: The Satara gecko reaches 60–70 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark, irregular transverse bands and a distinctive series of enlarged, keeled tubercles along the flanks. It lacks terminal scansors.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hemidactylus sataraensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark stripe running from the snout through the eye to the neck.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus sataraensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and cliffs within dry deciduous forests, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters in the Northern Western Ghats.
ai.behavior: The Satara gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its restricted range in the Northern Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus sataraensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus sataraensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
